+# CamCraft 0.21.0 (clean-room implementation)
+
+Released 2026-11-15.
+
+## Breaking
+None. No pull request in this release is marked breaking, and the project file
+format stays at version 61, so 0.20.0 opens files that 0.21.0 saves. Some posts
+and some toolpaths change for existing projects, though: read "Changes to posted
+programs" below before you post an old project again.
+
+A minor release headlined by **more wire and sinker EDM** (an outline
+electrode, Side Burn wear compensation, angle-word taper, 4-axis fan spans and
+sync picks, the Sodick ALC400G machine), **a 2D Adaptive Trochoidal method that
+clears wide and island regions**, **3D operations in part-aligned setups**,
+**stock carried into a setup turned side-on**, and **safer entries and setup
+changes in the posts**. 106 pull requests merged since 0.20.0 (19 features, 65
+fixes, 22 tests, docs and process).
+
+## Changes to posted programs
+These change the G-code that an existing project posts.
+- **Fanuc-family posts write a decimal point on whole-number values** (#1836,
+  PR #1866). Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan DNM and Fanuc lathe write `Z14.`, not
+  `Z14`, for each length, angle and feed-per-revolution word. A control with
+  parameter 3401#0 DPI=0 then no longer reads the word in least increments.
+- **G76 threading states the passes that were verified** (#417, PR #517). With
+  the G76 cycle option, the finish allowance R is posted: the default Fanuc lathe
+  thread now posts `R0.4` instead of `R0`. G32 passes stay the default output.
+- **Threading can repeat each roughing depth** (#418, PR #518). Off by default;
+  the G76 cycles refuse it by name.
+- **Seven mill posts retract Z and name the next setup before a setup-change
+  stop** (#1647, PR #1859). Heidenhain refuses a setup change without a safe work
+  clearance.
+- **The Tormach lathe approaches one axis at a time after G30** and leaves the
+  stock before each G30 (#1604, PR #1667).
+- **The Tormach mill skips a repeated G30/M6** when two sections in a row use the
+  same tool (#1626, PR #1741).
+- **grblHAL and TinyG** state indexed work offsets G54-G59 (#1385, PR #1824).
+  grblHAL, Carvera and TinyG write no motion after a refused first traverse
+  (#1682, PR #1707).
+- **Sodick wire posts** refuse an angle-word move and a control-side offset
+  request by name instead of posting them wrong (#1496, #1498).
+- Toolpath changes that show in the posted program:
+  - A Contour on an open edge of a part cuts with the tool on the air side, one
+    radius off the edge, not on the edge (#1777, PR #1781).
+  - Default Ramp entries of Inside Contour, Circular and Bore use 3 degrees, not
+    the link ramp angle (#1674). An inside Contour and a Bore with Ramp entry
+    descend at the ramp angle, not straight down at the cutting feed (#1664,
+    #1665).
+  - A whole-model 3D Pocket and Multi-Axis Rough clear out to the stock outline
+    and past an open-sided notch (#1774, #1749).
+  - Bore clears a wide hole with concentric rings (#1566).
+
+## Highlights
+### Posts and G-code
+- Optional plain-English Explain comments on the Tormach mill and the
+  Fanuc-family posts; the executable words do not change (#1387, #1388).
+- MCP lists the Tormach PathPilot Plasma post with its Plasma Profile workflow
+  (#1871).
+
+### Wire and sinker EDM
+- A sinker electrode can be a body with an outline, made from the cavity faces
+  (#1152). Rough and finish burns count the orbit radius (#1355). A Side Burn
+  takes a measured electrode wear and is compensated in Z (#1340). The Machine
+  window edits each condition's wear rate and notes (#1381).
+- Wire EDM: a machine can state an angle-word taper dialect (#1164); explicit
+  4-axis fan spans (#1172); pick the 4-axis sync points in the viewport (#1171);
+  skim order, holding tabs and captured-piece controls on the Passes tab
+  (#1148).
+- A wire taper that the machine cannot post is refused when you set it (#1800).
+  A user post script's Wire EDM manifest is honoured (#1335).
+- New built-in machine: Sodick ALC400G wire EDM, travels and taper from Sodick's
+  published specifications (#1501).
+
+### Operations
+- 2D Adaptive (Trochoidal) clears wide, branching, island and closed-ring areas
+  with parallel lanes and clean-up peels (#1587). Its engagement, return, return
+  feed and loop width are parameters (#1588).
+- 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset take a corner arc radius (#1733), cut the
+  band between two opposite open edges out to the stock (#1735), and accept a
+  U-shaped blind slot (#1762).
+- Slot: "Extend past A" and "Extend past B" (#1731).
+- Face, Contour, Pocket and 2D Adaptive take picked faces and edges in aligned
+  setups (#763). 3D Pocket, 3D Adaptive and 3D Finish work in part-aligned setups
+  (#1743).
+- The Boundary group takes edge picks in any pick mode; two edges bound the area
+  between them (#1727).
+- Tools can be assembled from modular multi-piece bodies from vendor STEP, STL
+  or OBJ models (#361).
+- Cross drill works on reduced-fidelity models with clearances widened by the
+  model's excess (#1053).
+
+### Gouge, collision and simulation
+- A setup turned side-on can take the machined stock of the setup before it; a
+  gouge cut before the turn stays in the verdict (#874).
+- An earlier setup's chamfers, deburrs and marks are credited before gouges are
+  kept (#1806). Engrave and Trace marks are credited only on the marked parts
+  (#1627).
+- 3D Pocket refuses a depth that the shank or holder cannot reach, and names
+  tool clearance when the open area is too narrow (#1844, #1709).
+- A stock band narrower than the tool is named (#1655). A stock-source 2D Chamfer
+  that breaks into a part names the cause and the workaround (#1637).
+- Ring ramps keep their planned chords (#1612). Rim crossings need a distance
+  band, so near-trace wall wobble stays under check (#1669).
+
+### Importers
+- A STEP closed shell that meshes open imports as an incomplete model with its
+  hole named; operations on it are refused at the post (#1610).
+- Runaway STEP edge and swept-curve subdivisions are refused by name (#1545).
+- Closed inward STL and OBJ bodies are turned outward at import (#1672).
+
+### UI
+- The workbench rework: denser built-in themes (PR #1639).
+- The Browser View shows the machine's work envelope (#1567).
+- The WCS marker pick anchors on part corners and circle or slot centres (#1502).
+- Hovering a picked feature marks its row in the Geometry tab (#1519). Pick
+  buttons share one style with a clear armed state (#1728). The first Ctrl+click
+  on a second edge adds it (#1726).
+- Machine page inputs carry accessibility labels (#1119). The CamCraft icon shows
+  in the Windows taskbar (#1754).
+
+### MCP
+- New tools: `get_post_options` and `set_post_options` (#1534), cylinder
+  alignment and setup origin placement (#1586).
+
+### Packaging and docs
+- The Linux RPM builds again (#1719).
+- Each of the 44 operation reference sections has a toolpath picture (#1250).
+  The user guide is grouped by job stage (#1903).
+
+## Not exercised on a real control
+No real control ran the output of these post changes. The test goldens are
+regression records. Check the first program on the machine before cutting.
+- The decimal point on Fanuc-family words (#1836): no control ran with DPI=0 or
+  DPI=1. The behaviour comes from the published parameter documentation.
+- G76 with the finish allowance R (#417): no Fanuc control run. That run is
+  tracked in #1842. The threading repeat pass (#418): no controller run.
+- Setup-change retract and stop on the seven mill posts (#1647).
+- The Tormach lathe G30 approach (#1604): no PathPilot lathe run. The Tormach
+  mill repeated-tool skip (#1626): no PathPilot or physical control run.
+- grblHAL and TinyG work offsets (#1385).
+- Wire and sinker EDM: the angle-word taper (#1164) and the Side Burn wear
+  compensation (#1340) use synthetic fixtures. The Sodick ALC400G output (#1501)
+  was not run on a Sodick control.
+
+## Process changes
+Contributor and agent process only; no effect on the program. PROCESS_VERSION
+went from 65 to 76:
+- **66** (PR #1693, PR #1704): the MCP skill documents `fit_stock`; the batch
+  gate runs the kernel suites; `gate --only` and `gate --failed`.
+- **67** (PR #1757): the post-merge gate has its own runner label.
+- **68** (PR #1718): the MCP skill documents `detect_holes` skipped holes and the
+  Bore refusal.
+- **69** (PR #1722, PR #1695): the MCP skill lists the post-options, cylinder
+  alignment and setup origin tools.
+- **70** (PR #1737): the release gate builds once and runs one heavy step for
+  each test binary.
+- **71** (PR #1744): the MCP skill covers modular multi-piece tool bodies.
+- **72** (PR #1790): the release gate runs independent lanes up to four at a time.
+- **73** (PR #1830): AGENTS.md is shorter and in ASD-STE100; procedures moved to
+  the `gate`, `runners`, `release-cut`, `fork-sync` and `issue-claims` skills.
+- **74** (PR #1823, PR #1835, PR #1878): committed review artifacts are removed
+  and refused; the release plan has kernel heavy steps.
+- **75** (PR #1899, PR #1900): `merge-ready` needs evidence of an independent
+  review; the MCP skill documents the plasma workflow.
+- **76** (PR #1919): the MCP skill states the bounded Bore ring rule of
+  `detect_holes`.
+

-a `G30`. The change is in that post only. The mill post `tormach.cps` does
-not change.
-
-- **After G30** (a tool change, or a "home" after-operation), the section's
-  first point is approached one axis at a time:
-  - The point is outside the stock's diameter: `G0 X<point>`, then
-    `G0 Z<point>`. X goes first.
-  - The point is inside the diameter but in front of the face: `G0 Z`, then
-    `G0 X`. The Z move goes to the point's Z. When the point is ON the face
-    (a hole's entry), the Z move goes to the section's `ClearancePlane`
-    first, then X, then Z down to the point.
-  - The point is inside the diameter and not in front of the face: refused
-    by name.
-- **Before G30** (a tool change, a "home" after-operation and the program
-  end), the tool leaves from the section's last point. It goes `G0 X` out
-  to the stock's diameter (when it is inside), then `G0 Z` out to the face
-  (when it is behind the face). When that corner is not clear of the stock
-  in either axis, the Z move goes to the `ClearancePlane`. These lines are
-  written before the next section's notes and work offset word, because the
-  words are in the old section's frame.
-- **The stock** is the section's `StockXYLeft/Right/Front/Back` box and
-  `StockZTop`, the parameters every stream already carries. The radius is
-  the box's largest half-width from the work-offset origin, and the face is
-  `StockZTop`. No new stream parameter is added.
-- **Refused by name:** no stock box, a first point inside the stock with no
-  `ClearancePlane` in front of the face, a section that ends inside the
-  stock's envelope, a section that ends on the stock's corner with no
-  `ClearancePlane`, and a feed, arc or thread half-turn as the first motion
-  after G30. After a refused approach, the post writes no motion until a
-  point is reached. This is the same rule as #1633.
-
-**Why.** LinuxCNC's G30 with no axis words moves every axis in one straight
-line to the stored position (parameters 5181-5189, from the public LinuxCNC
-G-code reference). The operator stores that position, so the post cannot
-know where the line goes. The approach is safe for every stored G30 outside
-the stock when each move stays outside the stock's diameter or in front of
-its face:
-- X first to a point outside the diameter: the X move runs at G30's Z. That
-  is in front of the face, or G30 is outside the diameter and the move stays
-  outside. The Z move then runs outside the diameter.
-- Z first to a point in front of the face: the Z move runs at G30's X. That
-  is outside the diameter, or G30 is in front of the face and the move stays
-  in front. The X move then runs in front of the face.

-  the face. A straight line from the corner to any point outside the stock
-  stays outside it. Thus the control's own G30 line cannot cross the stock.

-first, then Z. That order is kept for every point outside the stock's
-diameter: all turning and threading starts. For a hole on centre, X first
-from a G30 beside the bar moves into the bar. X first to a clearance
-diameter needs a radial clearance number, and the stream does not state
-one. A margin added by the post would be a guess. Z first, to the stated
-`ClearancePlane`, needs no guess, so the post uses it there.

-turret at G30, so the index happens at the operator's safe spot as before.
-On a gang plate the T word changes only the offsets, and the idle tools
-move with the slide. The post knows only the active tool's control point,
-so these rules protect that point only. The idle tools on a gang plate stay
-the operator's layout responsibility. The X-first rule keeps the slide's long Z move outside the
-stock's diameter, which is also the side where a gang plate's tools stand.

-## #1735 - Two open edges are the walls of a band that the stock outline closes
-
-**Decided:** A pocket-family operation (2D Offset, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive) whose selection holds two open edges of a part cuts the band between them. The definition is exact:
-
-- Picked open runs that share an end are welded into one wall. Exactly two walls, A and B, must remain. Each wall is level, and both walls are at one height (tolerance 0.001 mm).
-- Each wall is run on straight along the tangent at each of its ends.
-- S is the stock outline in XY, grown by the extension `e` with sharp corners.
-- `band(e) = (side of A that holds B) ∩ (side of B that holds A) ∩ S`.
-- `band(0)` is the region of the selection. The pocket region law then removes the standing material of the part at every cut plane, as it does for a closed pick.
-- `band(e)` is a lane. The area law clips its result to the lane after the extension step. Thus the extension moves the two open ends out of the stock along the walls. The extension does not widen the band, and the tool does not go round the end of a wall.
-
-A selection that does not give one clear band is refused by name: no stock; a wall that is not level; walls at different heights; walls at more than 45 degrees to each other; walls that do not run alongside each other; walls that cross or touch when run on; walls that run together inside the stock; a stock outline that does not cover the space between the walls; a stock outline that closes the band in more than one piece; more than two walls; open edges mixed with closed boundaries; open edges of the stock; three edges at one point. One open edge keeps the old refusal, word for word. Tool containment On or Outside is refused for a band, because the walls are the limit of the tool.
-
-**Why:** The maintainer reported it (issue 1735): two edges of a slot must give a path up to the stock edge, and "Extend past" must extend the reach out of the stock in the direction of the edges. An open slot or open pocket is bounded by its walls and by the stock in general 2.5D machining practice. The definition uses only half-plane splits and region intersections, so each result has one reading. No check was loosened: the region still loses the part's standing material, the operation still answers to the section gouge law and the solid law against the other parts of the setup, and a gouge still blocks the post. -- Run each wall out with Face's `extend_run_to_footprint` and union the two strips. Dropped: that law asks which side of one run holds the material; a band needs the side that holds the other wall.

-
-**What was decided.** The stock one setup leaves is carried through the
-sixteen side-on quarter turns (the old X or Y on the new tool axis) by a
-conservative read of the column body (`Body::carry_side`,
-`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`). The eight lattice turns keep
-their exact re-index. Every turn off the quarter turns keeps the named
-refusal (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`), with shorter words.
-
-The read, per new column:
-
-- The level axis that stays level is re-indexed, centre onto centre.
-- The old heights become a level axis in slabs of one cell. The slabs are
-  centred on the old Z range. An old column feeds every slab that its span
-  reaches into. A face inside a slab counts the slab whole.
-- The old level axis becomes the height. The new top and floor are the
-  hull of the old column centres that hold material in the slab. Each end
-  moves out to the next old centre that holds no material there, or to the
-  lattice edge. A cavity between the ends is filled.
-
-The carried body is never smaller than the body the columns hold. It is at
-most one grid cell larger on a turned face. The raw faces of a box stock at
-the lattice edge are read exactly.
-
-**A gouge cut before the turn is kept.** The hull can hide a gouge that an
-earlier setup cut (a face cut too deep becomes a wall that the new tool axis
-does not see). The program walk judges the body before a side-on turn and
-folds those gouges into the final verdict, the same fold a block left for a
-new block gets (#320). A gouge that both verdicts see is counted in both.
-
-**The floor is not judged after a side-on turn.** The new floor is a face
-the earlier setup held level, known to one cell. The gouges of the earlier
-setup are already kept by the fold above. A later flip sets the flag again.
-
-**The verdict says so.** The gate's note line names the first side-on carry
-and what the verdict reads (`side_on_note`).

-the tool axis. The shipped engine is the column engine.

-ordinary second setup. The refusal blocked it.
